Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 26-Dec-2024 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. (INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY/COMPUTER AND COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING) EXAMINATIONS -  
  DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: ICT 2121/IT_2121- DATA STRUCTURES  
  
  
Marks: 50                                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Write a C program that performs the following tasks on a circular linked list:                                       (5)  
  i) Create a circular linked list with at least 5 nodes based on user input.  
  ii) Find the first element greater than a given value in the list.  
  iii) Once such an element is found, insert two new elements (55 and 88):  
  a) Insert 55 before the element greater than the given value.  
  b) Insert 88 after the element greater than the given value.  
  
  If no such element is found, display a message indicating that no element greater than the given value exists.  
  Example Test Case:  
  If the input list is: 10, 22, 33, 44, 66 and the given value is 35,  
  The first element greater than 35 is 44. After inserting 55 before 44 and 88 after 44, the updated list should  
  become:  
  10, 22, 33, 55, 44, 88, 66  
1B)               Construct the binary tree if the inorder traversal is XPQLZFAMIGHN and preorder traversal is                         (3)  
  ZPXLQIMFANGH. Also write the level order traversal of the constructed binary tree.  
1C)               Write a user defined function to create the mirror image of a given binary tree.                                     (2)  
2A)               Write a program for a hospital patient management system where patients register at the reception and wait for (5)  
  their turn to see a doctor. The system processes patient entries in the order they register. It performs the  
  following operations:  
  
  Enqueue: A new patient registers and is added to the queue.  
  Dequeue: The first patient in the queue is called for consultation.  
  Front: Displays the next patient in line without removing them from the queue.  
  IsEmpty: Checks if there are any patients in the queue.  
  
2B)               Write a recursive program to find the sum of all the elements of an array.                                           (3)  
2C)               Develop a C program to read n integers and insert the numbers in a stack if the read integer is prime.               (2)  
3A)               It is proposed to develop an application that processes large datasets in scientific computing, where many           (5)  
  matrices are sparse. To optimize performance and memory usage, triplet format is used to represent these  
  matrices.  
  i) Discuss how using the triplet representation can affect the multiplication of sparse matrices compared to the  
  standard matrix form. In the answer, include considerations of:  
  
  a) Memory efficiency  
  b) Ease of access to non-zero elements  
  
  ii) Write a C program to multiply two sparse matrices represented in triplet form. The program should take the  
  
  triplet representations of both matrices as input and return the triplet representation of the resulting matrix,  
  including the row indices, column indices, and value.  
3B)               Convert the following infix expression to both prefix and postfix notations using stack:                             (3)  
  Infix Expression:  
  ((9 * (4 + 2)) / 3 + 8) * 2 - (15 - (2 + 3) * (4 + 5))                                                              Page 1 of 2

((9 * (4 + 2)) / 3 + 8) * 2 - (15 - (2 + 3) * (4 + 5))  
  i) Clearly show the steps taken to convert the infix expression to postfix notation.  
  ii) Clearly show the steps taken to convert the infix expression to prefix notation.  
  iii) Provide the final postfix and prefix expressions.  
3C)   Discuss the differences between full binary trees and complete binary trees. Provide at least four distinct points (2)  
  of comparison, focusing on their definitions, structures, node counts, and applications.  
4A)   Suppose you are given the following nodes to insert into a right-threaded binary tree (where right NULL              (5)  
  pointers are threaded to the in-order successor if it exists): 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80.  
  i) Draw the threaded binary tree after inserting these nodes in the given order.  
  ii) Examine the traversal path for an in-order traversal using the threads in the tree.  
4B)   Evaluate the following postfix expression                                                                            (3)  
  3 4 5 * + 6 2 / 7 2 * + - 9 8 - * showing all the intermediate steps.  
4C)   Write C snippet to find the length of a string using recursion by using static variable.                             (2)  
5A)                                                                                                                              (5)  
  
  
5B)   Write a C snippet to accept ten integers as inputs from the user and insert each integer into a singly linked list   (3)  
  only if it is a positive number and display the linked list after all valid inputs are inserted.  
5C)   State which type of linked lists you would apply for the following applications                                      (2)  
  a) Web browsers which use a linked list to manage the history of visited websites. Users can go "back" and  
  "forward" by traversing the list.  
  b) Operating systems which use linked lists to manage processes in a round-robin fashion for task scheduling.  
  
  
  -----End-----
